explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/4: for any C > 0, are there infinitely many n with p_{n+1} − p_n > C·(log log n · log log log log n)/(log log log n)²·log n? `Erdos4For C` states exactly this, with the term order rearranged, `Nat.nth Nat.Prime` as the 0-indexed prime sequence (an index shift is immaterial here) and real logarithms. The page records it as solved by Maynard and Ford–Green–Konyagin–Tao. Faithful.
